description: Local-first developer workbench for exploring and transforming large JSON data, shipped as a Chrome extension (plus CLI and VS Code packages).

cwsListing.shortDescription: Inspect, transform, validate, diff, and query large JSON locally. Nothing leaves your browser.
cwsListing.detailedDescription: JSON Workbench is a local-first developer tool for large JSON, JSONL, and NDJSON files. Open a file, a JSON tab, or a captured response and explore it as a tree or table without losing numeric precision. Profile structure, infer a JSON Schema, build reproducible transform pipelines (native steps, jq, and JSONata), run local DuckDB SQL, diff two payloads as an RFC 6902 JSON Patch (with a side-by-side visual view), and export JSON, JSONL, CSV, or TSV. It can also pretty-print any JSON page in place. Your source data stays in the browser. Works in Chrome and Edge 120+.
cwsListing.singlePurpose: JSON Workbench lets developers inspect, transform, validate, diff and query JSON data locally in the browser.
cwsListing.remoteCodeJustification: The extension does not execute remote code. All scripts and WebAssembly runtimes (DuckDB WASM, jq) are bundled into the extension package.

permissionJustifications.activeTab: Reads JSON from the active tab only when the user explicitly asks to open or format it.
permissionJustifications.sidePanel: Displays the workbench interface in Chrome's side panel.
permissionJustifications.storage: Persists local preferences and transform pipelines on the device.
permissionJustifications.scripting: Injects the in-page JSON formatter into the active tab upon explicit user request.
permissionJustifications.debugger: Optional; requested only if the user opts in to capturing network JSON responses, which stay in local memory.
